subject: Re: Post-call: Finex throughput & latency qualification - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Kyle Park <kyle.park@finex.com>, Nicole Turner <nicole.turner@finex.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — throughput / latency questions

Hi Kyle / Nicole,

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate the walkthrough of Finex's summarization pipeline and the latency targets. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

- Latency SLO: 95th percentile end-to-end inference <= 300ms for interactive web experience (you confirmed this is the target for agent UI).
- Model: 13B open model (CPU/GPU-optimized variant) with streaming enabled for partial responses.
- Steady-state: ~150 concurrent users during business hours; average request = 600 tokens (including prompt + response).
- Peak bursts: up to 600 concurrent users for 20-30 minute windows during market open; expect ~2.5x token/sec increase.
- Desired throughput metric: tokens/sec and QPS per model variant; also want tokens/sec per GPU.

Next steps I propose:
1) You send the load profile CSV (tokens per request distribution + expected concurrency windows) — Nicole offered to share that.
2) Rafael will run a quick sizing estimate and provide recommended GPU pool (cards + expected tokens/sec) and a cost ballpark.
3) We'll validate streaming constraints (minimum chunk size, time-to-first-byte) and confirm if partial-response streaming counts toward your 300ms P95.

Can you confirm timeline for the CSV? If you can share the load profile today/tomorrow we can get a sizing back by Monday.

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

From: Kyle Park <kyle.park@finex.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nicole Turner <nicole.turner@finex.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 09:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — throughput / latency questions

Marissa — thanks, great recap. Attaching the load profile CSV (finex_load_profile.csv) and our SLO doc (slo_requirements.pdf). A few clarifications inline:

- The 300ms P95 is measured from client-to-client (so network + app + inference). For sizing we recommend you assume 100ms application overhead and 50ms network, leaving ~150ms for inference at P95.
- Average tokens per request: 600 as you noted; 90th percentile request size is ~1,600 tokens.
- Steady-state concurrency: 120 users typical; peak concurrency up to 550 for 10-25 minute burst windows (market open / close).
- Burst profile: token arrival rate roughly 2.8x steady state for 15 minutes.
- Streaming: we stream partial responses; we care about TTFB <= 120ms for first chunk, and subsequent chunk spacing <= 50ms.

Let us know if you need additional telemetry fields (per-request RTT) — we can extract and share sample logs.

Best,
Kyle
VP Product — Finex Solutions
kyle.park@finex.com

[Attachment: finex_load_profile.csv]
[Attachment: slo_requirements.pdf]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 11:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — throughput / latency questions

Marissa — thanks for the ping and Kyle for the data. I skimmed the CSV and SLO doc. Quick notes before I run sizing: 

- We should differentiate tokens/sec per GPU vs tokens/sec per serving cluster. For the 13B model on A100-like hardware, our baseline single-GPU sustained generation is ~1,200 tokens/sec for greedy streaming at typical beam=1 settings. Quantization/optimizations could push that toward ~1,800 t/s but increases latency variance.
- For P95 inference <=150ms (inference-only budget), we need to keep per-request decode time low. Streaming helps with TTFB but increases overhead for many small chunks — Neha, can you factor in chunk size config options (64 vs 128 tokens) in the sim?
- Given the 550 concurrent peak with 1,600-token 90th pct requests, if many requests are long we need autoscale headroom. I'll produce two sizing scenarios: conservative (target P95 at peak) and cost-optimized (target P95 at steady + graceful degradation on peak).

I'll aim to have draft numbers Monday EOD PST.

- Rafael
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.ai

Kyle / Nicole — looping back with next steps and a quick checklist while Rafael completes sizing: 

- Action items for Finex:
  * Confirm whether the client counts streaming partial chunks toward the 300ms P95 (important for how we measure).
  * Share sample logs if you want token-level RTT included in the analysis.

- Nothing blocking from Redwood — Rafael will send sizing + recommended GPU pool and expected tokens/sec per GPU.

Proposed deliverables (what you'll get from us):
- Sizing doc with two scenarios (conservative vs cost-optimized)
- Suggested autoscaling policy (min nodes, burst headroom, cooldowns)
- Streaming tuning recommendations (chunk size, flush interval)
- Example dashboard metrics to monitor (P50/P95 latency, tokens/sec per GPU, queue depth)

Can you confirm that sample logs are ok to share? If so, Rafael can include a short validation run against a representative sample.

Thanks — talk soon.

--
Marissa Cole

Also: preference is cost-optimized with graceful degradation on peak — we want to avoid paying for peak capacity 24/7 if we can accept slightly higher P95 during 15-minute bursts.

Cheers,
Kyle
